name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
what: Org context assembled from the M365 graph — mail, files, chat, calendar, identity — and surfaced across Office, Teams, and Copilot Studio.
relationship: Owns the identity layer, the file layer, and the procurement relationship at almost every enterprise Coconut wants. The buyer's default question is not 'is Coconut better' but 'why is this not just Copilot'.
coconut_answer: Model-agnostic and not locked to the Microsoft estate. Real, but a harder sell to a CIO already paying for E5.

name: ChatGPT Memory / Company Knowledge
what: Persistent memory plus connectors inside ChatGPT. Context is a property of the tool, configured per workspace, and improves with every model release at no extra line item.
relationship: The single largest structural risk. Coconut's whole argument is that context must live outside any one tool. That argument only pays if buyers actually run multiple AI vendors. Every month ChatGPT's own memory gets better, the marginal buyer asks why they are paying a second vendor for something bundled.
coconut_answer: Model-agnostic portability, and the claim that context is an organizational asset you own rather than a tool configuration you rent.

name: Claude Projects / Cowork
what: Project-scoped knowledge, Skills, and MCP connectors inside Claude and Cowork. Anthropic authors the MCP standard Coconut's distribution depends on.
relationship: Still the most uncomfortable entry, but narrower than on 2026-08-08. The August reading rested on a supply-chain dependency: Coconut ran Claude Code inside its own instances and shipped skills through the Claude Code plugin marketplace against Anthropic's SKILL.md spec. None of that exists in the product documented at docs.coconut.md — no skills, no marketplace, no SKILL.md, no coding agent. What remains is the ordinary exposure every MCP-native company carries: Anthropic owns the protocol and sells a product one layer up whose every improvement narrows the gap Coconut sells into.
coconut_answer: Coconut is the governed org layer Claude Projects is not — owners, ACLs, append-only revisions, a metadata query engine, and reach across every tool. The land is less rented than it was in August, but the protocol is still Anthropic's.

name: Notion AI
what: AI inside the workspace where a great many teams already keep their docs, wikis, and trackers, with enterprise search extending to external connectors.
relationship: Path of least resistance. Coconut lists Notion as a source connector, which means for a Notion-native org Coconut is arguing it should sit above the tool that already holds the knowledge and already sells an AI add-on.
coconut_answer: Governance depth and model-agnostic distribution. Notion AI is ecosystem-locked.

name: Amdahl
what: Intelligent context layer / context backbone for AI agents, focused on go-to-market. Ships an MCP server plus a Claude plugin, and serves the most-relevant context with citations rather than the raw MCP firehose.
relationship: Same 'context layer' language, narrowed to GTM. Vertical focus is the standard way to beat a horizontal platform in a specific department, and GTM is one of Coconut's named segments.
coconut_answer: Coconut spans Leadership, Investors, and Operating Functions rather than one motion.

name: Hyperspell
what: Connects tools and synthesizes documents and conversations into a live, permissioned context graph.
relationship: Surfaced during verification as another company-brain entrant. Permissioned context graph is the same primitive. Listed for completeness; not independently profiled.
coconut_answer: n/a — insufficient verification to draw a contrast.

name: Hyper
founders: Shalin Shah, Kanyes Thaker — San Francisco
what: Self-driving company brain. Ingests Docs, Slack, Email, Calendar, GitHub, and Granola into a self-maintaining knowledge graph, then injects context into Claude Code, Cursor, and ChatGPT via MCP on every prompt turn. Facts carry provenance, staleness tracking, and per-user access control.
relationship: The closest functional twin and the primary benchmark. Provenance, staleness, per-user access and MCP injection are Coconut's governance pitch, shipped by a team with public traction. As of 2026-08-18 both companies publish their retrieval architecture, and the contrast is stark: Hyper runs query expansion plus reciprocal rank fusion over embeddings and Postgres full-text search with a ZeroEntropy reranker; Coconut runs Postgres full-text search, with no embeddings, no vector store and no reranker anywhere in 27 pages of documentation.
coconut_answer: Not breadth any more — the VM instances, coding agent and skills shelf are gone. What is left is a different bet: that enterprise questions are state questions rather than semantic ones, and that a typed, audited, queryable metadata layer answers them exactly where retrieval answers them probabilistically. Defensible, and nowhere argued in public. Coconut also has documented self-hosting and a space-template gallery; Hyper has neither.

name: Cerenovus
founders: Lucas Baur, Oliver Moreland, Jonathan Waldorf — San Francisco
what: Aggregates files, PDFs, emails, Slack, spreadsheets, and meeting notes into a single Markdown-based knowledge graph with native AI-agent integration. Maps the company as a system — people, processes, tools — and infers where operations are inefficient.
relationship: The closest architectural match of anyone: Markdown-first knowledge graph, agent-native, and an explicit systems map of the company. Where Coconut has a fixed five-layer taxonomy, Cerenovus infers the structure. If inference works, Coconut's opinionated schema becomes a setup cost rather than a feature.
coconut_answer: Coconut has a shipped 1.0, an API, a CLI, deployment options, and a named enterprise reference. Cerenovus has three founders and pilots.

name: Savant
founders: Anthony Kim (CEO), Kevin Yu (CTO) — San Francisco
what: Operational memory layer. Plugs into existing tools to capture written knowledge and undocumented procedures, then serves them to employees and agents at decision time.
relationship: Same thesis, different wedge: Savant leads with undocumented procedures — the tribal knowledge nobody wrote down — where Coconut leads with structuring what already exists. Capturing the undocumented is the harder and more defensible half.
coconut_answer: Coconut's space agents fold transcripts into memos, which attacks the same problem from the other end.

name: Memory Store
founders: Diwank Tomer (Thiel Fellow), Ishita Jindal — San Francisco, 4 employees
what: One shared memory for teammates and agents. Collects from Slack, Gmail, and Granola, synthesizes a company brain, keeps it current, and exposes it to any MCP client. Self-updating 'Briefs' are living docs that rewrite themselves as new memories land.
relationship: Briefs are functionally Coconut's living pages. The founders previously built Julep, an open-source agent orchestrator with 7K+ stars, so they have shipped infrastructure at this layer before and arrive with distribution.
coconut_answer: Coconut's governance surface — owners, versions, lineage, rollback — is deeper than a self-updating doc.

name: Glen
what: Unified organizational context for every agent and human. Reads code, PRs, issues, docs, and meetings, reconciles them, and gives agents the full picture instead of one slice. Distills completed work into reusable skills.
relationship: Distilling finished work back into skills is exactly Coconut's Skills loop. One employee, so this is a directional signal about where the category converges, not a live threat.
coconut_answer: Coconut already ships this loop with a skills registry and a marketplace.

name: Corvera
what: Context layer for AI-native CPG brands. Makes a brand's unified data legible to any AI tool via MCP.
relationship: Evidence that the horizontal context layer is already fragmenting into verticals. Not a competitor to Coconut directly, but a preview of how the category gets carved up.
coconut_answer: n/a — different buyer.

name: GBrain
what: Open-source, Markdown-first, self-wiring knowledge-graph memory for AI agents. Local-first: Markdown files in git plus Postgres with pgvector. Ships as an MCP server. Nightly 'dream cycle' consolidates memory. Multi-user company-brain mode.
relationship: The price floor, and the reason Coconut cannot win on architecture alone. Same Markdown-first, git-versioned, MCP-served design, free, and authored by the person who runs the accelerator funding Coconut's closest rivals. 28,015 stars and 4,102 forks as of 2026-08-08, created only 2026-04-05 — that is four months to a number Coconut's own repos will not reach.
coconut_answer: Managed connectors, permissions enforced for you, and someone to call at 2am — now backed by documented Docker Compose, Helm and Terraform deployment paths, which is a stronger self-host story than most commercial rivals offer. The same documentation teaches a capable buyer how to price building it. Coconut must still price below the engineering cost of self-hosting GBrain for a 25-50 person team.

name: Palantir AIP
what: Enterprise data and AI platform built on an explicit ontology of the business.
relationship: Palantir has been selling 'model your company as a structured ontology so software can act on it' for two decades. Coconut's five layers are a lightweight, self-serve version of the same conviction. The relevant lesson is that this sale is slow, consultative, and expensive.
coconut_answer: Days to value, not quarters. That is the whole difference and it must hold up in a pilot.

name: Moveworks
what: Enterprise agentic AI copilot and search across Slack, Teams, and ServiceNow, with an agentic reasoning engine.
relationship: The proof that this category exits into platform vendors. Announced March 2025, cleared a DOJ second request, closed December 15 2025 — the largest acquisition in ServiceNow's history. Read it two ways: platform vendors will buy rather than build, and a Coconut-shaped company has a credible exit.
coconut_answer: Not a head-to-head rival now, but it sets the price and the pattern.

name: Stack Internal (Stack Overflow)
what: Private Q&A rebranded as an enterprise knowledge intelligence layer, with an MCP server giving OAuth-secured read/write access to verified knowledge for Copilot, ChatGPT, Cursor, JetBrains, and M365.
relationship: The closest incumbent on Coconut's exact combination of MCP distribution plus verified, governed knowledge. Human verification of answers remains a governance primitive Coconut does not have: propose-then-publish review is absent from both of Coconut's documentation sites as of 2026-08-18.
coconut_answer: Coconut covers all org knowledge, not developer Q&A.

name: Glean
what: Permissions-aware enterprise search over a knowledge graph, plus Glean Agents. Positions its knowledge graph as the governed context layer for enterprise AI agents. Model-agnostic.
relationship: The comparison every enterprise buyer will make, and the gap is wider than prior research suggested. ARR went from ~$100M to $208M at end-2025 to $300M by May 2026 — an 89% year-over-year jump. Glean is not a slow incumbent to be out-executed; it is compounding faster than most startups in the category.
coconut_answer: Glean helps people find information; Coconut lets agents query state. Genuinely different jobs — but Glean Agents is closing that distance, and Glean already has the connector library, the ACL enforcement and the procurement relationships. Coconut's newer answers are self-hosting and a solutions-template gallery, neither of which Glean sells.

name: ClickUp Brain
what: Native AI layer inside ClickUp drawing on tasks, docs, and projects.
relationship: Workspace-bound, not model-agnostic. Same bundling logic as Notion AI at a smaller scale.
coconut_answer: Portability.

name: Capacity
what: AI support-automation platform assembled from acquisitions, including Starmind's expertise network.
relationship: A roll-up of knowledge and support tooling. Adjacent rather than competing, but it is buying the pieces Coconut is building.
coconut_answer: Different buyer — support ops rather than the AI platform owner.

name: PromptQL (Hasura)
what: Trusted, accurate LLM access to business data using Hasura metadata and API-layer security. Multiplayer AI with shared threads and wiki. MCP server available.
relationship: Solves deterministic metric governance over the warehouse — the flank Coconut does not cover. Coconut governs prose and process; PromptQL governs numbers. A complement, but enterprises will probe the seam.
coconut_answer: Partner rather than compete. Pre-empt the 'can it do governed metrics' objection.

name: DevRev
what: AI-native support and product platform built on AgentOS over a real-time knowledge graph.
relationship: Knowledge-graph-backed agent platform, but anchored to support and product workflows rather than org-wide context.
coconut_answer: Different surface area.

name: Contextual AI
what: Enterprise platform for building specialized RAG agents, with a grounded language model and reranker. Founded by ex-FAIR researchers.
relationship: A platform for teams that want to build their own context system. Competes for the same budget with the opposite answer: build it yourself on better primitives.
coconut_answer: Coconut is the finished product, not the toolkit.

name: Guru
what: AI knowledge management and enterprise search with verification workflows, permission-aware cited answers, and a browser extension.
relationship: Guru shipped verification intervals and content ownership years before anyone called it a context layer. Coconut's decay signals and last-verified are the same idea rebuilt for agents. Guru has the install base; Coconut has the agent-native design.
coconut_answer: Guru is a knowledge base with AI bolted on. Coconut is context-first and model-agnostic.

name: Shelf.io
what: AI knowledge management and answer automation for contact centers.
relationship: Contact-center vertical. Shares the 'stale knowledge is a liability' thesis with a different buyer.
coconut_answer: Different segment.

name: Dust
what: Multiplayer AI platform for human-agent collaboration. Connects agents to company knowledge across 100+ data sources with built-in memory, feedback loops, and enterprise governance.
relationship: Badly underrated in prior research, which listed it only as 'VC-backed'. The $40M Series B was led by Abstract and Sequoia with Snowflake Ventures and Datadog participating, and Dust reports 3,000+ organizations at 70%+ weekly active usage. Note the language: Dust made 'multiplayer AI' a category term in May 2026, and Coconut's blog adopted the same framing on July 31 2026.
coconut_answer: Coconut is a context layer that feeds any tool; Dust is a workspace you work inside. But Dust has memory, governance, and 100+ connectors, and it got there first with real distribution.

name: Sana
what: AI knowledge assistant, enterprise search, and agent builder.
relationship: Second data point in the consolidation wave. Workday framed it as building a new front door for work, folding Sana's search and agents into people and money context — the same 'context layer owned by the system of record' move Coconut has to argue against.
coconut_answer: Coconut is not tied to one system of record, which is the whole pitch.

name: Bloomfire
what: Knowledge engagement and AI knowledge management platform.
relationship: Install base to displace rather than a competitor to beat.
coconut_answer: Not AI-native.

name: Dashworks
what: AI enterprise search and internal Q&A assistant across work apps.
relationship: Another consolidation data point. The HubSpot acquisition is carried from prior research and was not independently confirmed for this report.
coconut_answer: n/a

name: Starmind
what: AI expertise network mapping who-knows-what inside an organization — tacit and human knowledge rather than documents.
relationship: Attacks the half of tribal knowledge that never gets written down — the gap in every document-centric context layer, Coconut's included.
coconut_answer: Coconut's Relationships layer gestures at this but is populated from documents, not from who actually answers questions.

name: Osseus
what: Secure research brain for R&D teams. Permissioned, version-aware memory connecting CAD, schematics, BOMs, firmware, simulations, tests, and supplier feedback for robotics and hardware R&D.
relationship: The single most relevant company to the robotics-stack question. Osseus occupies the slot a robotics-native Coconut would occupy, and it is already taken. Permissioned and version-aware over engineering artifacts is Coconut's governance model applied to hardware.
coconut_answer: Coconut is not in this market. Osseus shows what entering it would require: CAD, BOM, and firmware-aware connectors, not Slack and Drive.

name: ZoomInfo GTM AI
what: Agent-native / headless GTM context layer delivered via MCP or a single API.
relationship: A public company marketing the exact phrase 'context layer for agents'. Evidence the language is being claimed fast, which weakens it as positioning real estate.
coconut_answer: Own 'governance-first' rather than 'context layer' alone.

name: Almanac
funding_display: ~$43M raised · US entity shut down Jan 2025
what: Docs and wiki positioned as an OS for remote work.
relationship: A cautionary tale worth more than most of the live competitors: $43M into org-knowledge tooling that could not find a durable wedge before AI reset the category.
coconut_answer: n/a

name: Slite
what: Team knowledge base with AI Ask and stale-doc detection, connecting to 20+ tools with human approval.
relationship: Stale-doc detection plus human approval is a lightweight version of Coconut's decay signals and tiered propagation — shipped, in a cheaper product.
coconut_answer: Coconut's version is agent-facing and governed at the page level.

name: Slab
what: Modern knowledge base and wiki with unified search.
relationship: Install base.
coconut_answer: n/a

name: Tettra
what: Internal knowledge base and wiki with Slack AI Q&A.
relationship: Prior generation of the same instinct.
coconut_answer: n/a

name: Mintlify
what: AI-native documentation platform with docs optimized to serve AI agents. Acquired Trieve in 2025.
relationship: Worth noting for one reason: Coconut's own documentation is built and hosted on Mintlify. A supplier, and a company moving toward docs-as-agent-context from the other direction.
coconut_answer: Different scope — public docs, not internal org context.

name: LangChain / LlamaIndex
what: The dominant LLM orchestration and RAG frameworks.
relationship: Named in the AI stack map at Layer 9, where Coconut also has real presence. Frameworks, not managed platforms.
coconut_answer: Coconut is a product; these are parts.

name: Swimm
what: Continuous, auto-synced code documentation for engineering teams.
relationship: Auto-synced docs that decay-check themselves — Coconut's freshness thesis applied narrowly to code.
coconut_answer: Coconut spans the whole org, not the repo.

name: Mem0
what: Open-source memory layer for AI apps. Three-tier memory across user, session, and agent, over a hybrid vector, graph, and key-value store. Self-editing memory model.
relationship: Named in the AI stack map at Layer 10 as the memory player — the slot Coconut is arguing it belongs in. 62,829 stars means Mem0 owns developer mindshare for 'AI memory' outright, and a technical buyer starts there.
coconut_answer: Mem0 is a library for builders with no governance layer; Coconut is a governed org system with an ACL engine, append-only revisions and audited metadata. Different buyer, same words — and note that Coconut is now explicitly not a vector store, so the two no longer even compete on mechanism.

name: Zep
what: Long-term memory for conversational AI with episodic and temporal memory and entity extraction.
relationship: Named alongside Mem0 in the AI stack map's Layer 10. Narrow: conversation memory, not org knowledge.
coconut_answer: Different scope entirely.

name: Letta (MemGPT)
what: Open-source, model-agnostic stateful agent runtime with tiered core, recall, and archival memory.
relationship: Solves memory at the runtime layer beneath Coconut. A complement in principle; a substitute for a team that would rather build.
coconut_answer: Coconut is the org layer above the runtime.

name: Cognee
what: Open-source graph memory for AI agents with auto-extracted ontologies, provenance tracking, and MCP support.
relationship: Auto-extracted ontologies are the counter-argument to Coconut's fixed five-layer schema: let structure emerge rather than imposing it.
coconut_answer: Opinionation is the product for non-technical teams who do not want to design a schema.

name: Quivr
what: Open-source RAG framework for building second brains and GenAI assistants over your documents. Model-agnostic, self-hostable.
relationship: 39,393 stars and no commits in over a year. The clearest evidence in this dataset that stars are not traction and that build-your-own-second-brain projects decay. Useful ammunition for Coconut's managed pitch.
coconut_answer: Maintenance is the product.

name: Kapa.ai
what: Turns technical documentation into AI assistants via RAG over 30+ sources.
relationship: Narrow docs-QA.
coconut_answer: n/a

name: Screenpipe
what: Records screen and audio continuously and locally, turning it into searchable memory, SOPs, and agent context. Open source with MCP and an API.
relationship: The opposite philosophy: capture everything automatically versus curate deliberately. If passive capture proves good enough, curation looks like unnecessary labour. The governance and privacy objections that come with it are Coconut's best counter.
coconut_answer: Curate-first produces something an owner can stand behind. Capture-first produces a haystack.

name: Langbase
what: Serverless AI agent platform with managed semantic memory across 250+ models, marketing context-engineered agents.
relationship: Infrastructure layer, uses the same vocabulary.
coconut_answer: n/a

name: Epicenter
what: Open-source, local-first ecosystem of apps sharing one plain-text and SQLite memory.
relationship: Personal, not org-governed. Shares the plain-text-as-substrate conviction.
coconut_answer: No multi-user governance.
